newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of April 14, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Computer Associates International Inc is scheduled to release this summer its upgrade for OpenIngres database which analysts said was a credible competitor of Microsoft's SQL Server. Oracle Corp also is upgrading its database, the Oracle8, PCWeek reported April 14.
IBM Corp and Netscape Communications also have released Web development tools that may woo programers away from Microsoft, PCWeek said.

COMPUTERWORLD - Oracle Corp will stop support for all versions of its application package that are not Year 2000-compliant. Users will either have to migrate to the latest version of the business application package 10.7, the only version that is completely year 100 compliant.
This move will affect almost all of Oracle's 3,700 users, according to the April 14 edition of Computerworld.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - The bundling of computer products and services is making a comeback at large systems vendors like International Business Machines Corp, which is offering packaged deals that include everything from servers to PCs to financing to services, CRN reported April 14.
Microsoft Corp is planning to package its Normandy Internet services with BackOffice, making them available to value-added resellers.

Before this package, the services have been available only to large Internet service providers and telecoms. Now the company plans to broaden reach to the intranet and extranet markets. The new services will be called Olympus, Computer Reseller News reported April 14.

INFOWORLD - Microsoft Corp plans to split its Windows NT operating system into three versions for large enterprises, general business and consumers after next year's release of version 5.0, InfoWorld reported April 14.
Netscape Communications Corp and International Business Machines Corp will announce technology agreements this quarter aimed at bringing legacy data to intranet applications, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - Compaq Computer Corp has emerged as a third member of the partnership between Microsoft and Intel Corp that dominates the personal computer industry, Information Week reported April 14.

Hewlett-Packard Co next month will unveil a line of very high-end Unix servers dubbed V-Class that will take aim at Sun Microsystems Inc's E10000 mainframe alternative, Information Week reported April 14.

EE TIMES - There could be a stumbling block to Memphis, Microsoft's successor to the Windows 95 operating system, because of a slow transition to the company's new generation of 32-bit Windows driver technology, EE Times said in its April 14 issue.
PC makers said some key technologies will not be supported until the company ships Memphis and the 5.0 release of Windows NT expected next year.
ELECTRONIC BUYERS NEWS - Toshiba Corp made serious moves towards diversifying beyond DRAMs last week when it said it would start a division dedicated to proprietary, single-chip memory-logic devices.

It also plans to make new chips in Japan, shifting from ASICs and other traditional logic devices made at the Oita, Japan, site. The company rolled out last week its 0.25-micron 1T DRAM ASIC family, Electronic Buyers news reported April 14.

MAC WEEK - Apple Computer demonstrated its future high-performance machine, the Power Mac 9600/410, at the recent National Association of Broadcasters show under the guise of a third-party technology demonstration, MacWeek reported April 14.
Power Computing Corp is poised to launch in May the first of two PowerCenter Pro models with a 60-MHz system bus, MacWeek reported.
INTERACTIVE WEEK - In an effort to make commerce on the Internet safe and secure, insurers are stepping into the fray to cover the risk.

U.S. Fidelity & Guaranty Co plans to announce a deal in which it will provide insurance for online purchases using Verisign Inc digital identification technology. The insurer initially will underwrite policies offering coverage for up to $25,000 in losses that stem from theft, impersonation or loss of a digital identification, Interactive Week reported April 14.
